tutorial.alone_mechanical.title: Alone Mechanical · Field Guide
tutorial.alone_mechanical.tooltip: Right-click to open the field guide
tutorial.alone_mechanical.start.title: Getting started
tutorial.alone_mechanical.start.body:
New here? Start with the guide book, engineering hammer and wrench. Right-click the book; hold Shift on an item to see what it does and what it needs.

For your first machine, place the shell, core, controller and storage. Use the wrench to set each port channel, then right-click two opposite corners with the hammer. If formation fails, the chat message names the missing part and its position.

Picked the wrong corner? Sneak-right-click to cancel. Once a machine is formed, right-click any block in it for the GUI. After changing coils, matrices or storage, right-click the old area with the hammer to validate it again.

Use JEI for recipes, quantities and current numbers. This guide focuses on the order of operations; JEI tells you how many items to use.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.grid.title: Power grid
tutorial.alone_mechanical.grid.body:
Power the machines first, then automate them. Put the grid core somewhere easy to reach; signal poles extend the line and power pylons feed machines. None of these blocks generates power. Place a generator beside the core or connect compatible FE equipment.

There are three steps to wiring: open a node GUI, click Start linking, then right-click the target. Repeat a link to remove it; sneak-right-click while selecting to cancel. Pole/core links reach %s blocks and pylons reach %s blocks, measured in three-dimensional distance.

A pylon covers %s×%s blocks horizontally and %s blocks above and below its base. Coverage is checked at the industrial core. Keep the route chunks loaded, then check the machine FE buffer; stored FE can keep it running briefly after a disconnect.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.structure.body:
Think of a multiblock as a workshop with walls, a core and a control panel. Build a complete cuboid, with every edge between 3 and %s blocks. Casings, structural glass, coils and matrices can make the shell.

Place one controller on the shell and the matching industrial core inside. The core does not have to be centered, but it must be inside the selection. Put the machine component directly above it. Add at least one energy matrix and keep storage columns inside the selection.

Ports belong directly above or below their storage columns. Set Input 1, Input 2, Output 1 or Output 2 with the wrench before selecting two corners with the hammer. If a column count, channel or shell block is wrong, the formation message tells you the exact reason.

Use exactly one component directly above the core: industrial + forging → forging press; smelting + calcination → arc furnace; smelting + alloy → alloy smelter; reaction + combination → reactor; reaction + decomposition → separator. Crusher/industrial core + conversion components still work directly. Legacy alloy/industrial core + decomposition components cannot form.

Industrial cores also support forming and infusion components directly above them, selecting a forming machine or infuser.

Tower exception: distillation and condensation require at least 5x5x7 with open tops. Exchange has a sealed roof and complete casing divider. All tower floors and frames require casings; ports connect directly without tanks. See Process Towers.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.machines.title: Item processing
tutorial.alone_mechanical.machines.body:
Start with a crusher: put raw ore in Item Input 1 and connect Item Output 1 to a vault. Crushers and arc furnaces both need two separate item columns with at least 27 slots each. A crusher turns raw iron, copper or gold into two dust; an arc furnace uses the smelting recipes currently loaded.

Once you have dust, build an alloy smelter. It always has three columns: main material in Input 1, additive in Input 2 and product in Output 1. Steel is 2 iron dust + 1 carbon dust -> 2 steel ingots.

When a machine stops, check in this order: formation, pylon coverage, port channels, output space and the JEI recipe. Empty-hand right-click any formed block to open its GUI.

Forging press: industrial core with a forging component directly above. Separate Input 1/Output 1 vault columns need 27 slots each; other shell/controller/matrix/port rules match the crusher. Default recipes press iron, copper and steel ingots into matching plates 1:1; data packs use machine=alone_mechanical:forging_press.

Forming machine: industrial core + forming component above. Exactly two item columns: Input 1 and Output 1. Item-to-item processing; default recipes form one copper plate into four wires and two steel plates into one gear. 

Infuser: industrial core + infusion component above. Exactly three columns: item Input 1, fluid OR gas Input 2, item Output 1. One resource additive only; item additives and simultaneous fluid+gas inputs are rejected. Includes 14 dimension infusion recipes at 250 mB, 100 ticks and 40 FE/t per item; flowers and vines yield one of two Nether products at 50% each. Both follow common casing/controller/energy-matrix/top-bottom-port rules and use independent recipes.

Field machines: industrial core with slaughter/breeding/harvest/repeller component directly above. Fixed 3 x 3 footprint; normal machine height limit. Output 1 vault is required; breeding also needs food Input 1. Default configurable range: 17 x 9 x 17 centered on the core. GUI shows dimensions; goggles + Shift while looking shows a translucent red range. Slaughter defaults to no targets, selected in its GUI, with base 8 damage/s. Breeding respects food, cooldowns and population limits. Harvest reserves planting items and resets growth, pausing on full output. Repeller blocks hostile spawns without removing existing mobs. Standard upgrades apply.

Population settings: open Configure populations for a searchable nearby/configured species list, individual switches and limits. Shift-click +/- changes by 10. Enter or leaving a number field saves it; server confirmation shows Synced. Gas-producing machines offer Keep internally / Vent excess / Vent all per output in Gas output.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.reactors.title: Biphasic reactors
tutorial.alone_mechanical.reactors.body:
Use a industrial core + compound component with a combination component directly above, and exactly three independent columns: Input 1, Input 2 and Output 1, with universal ports directly above/below them.

Resource types select nine profiles:
Item + fluid → fluid: Dissolution
Item + fluid → item: Crystallization
Fluid + gas → fluid: Liquid capture
Fluid + gas → gas: Gas evolution
Item + gas → item: Gas-solid refining
Item + gas → gas: Solid gasification
Fluid + fluid → fluid: Liquid-phase synthesis
Gas + gas → gas: Gas-phase synthesis
Item + item → item: Solid fusion

Different input resource types may swap channels; recipes map them by type. For equal types, use recipe-specified channels. Formation messages and the GUI show the profile. Data packs provide reactions; arbitrary resources never react automatically.

Sulfur recovery, sulfur oxidation, SO2 oxidation and steam hydration recipes now form the sulfuric acid line. See Sulfuric Acid Line for all stages.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.conversion.bod:
Use a industrial core + conversion component with exactly one fluid tank column and one gas tank column, matching ports and at least one energy matrix. No vault is required.

Use Input 1 and Output 1 only. Gas input/fluid output selects liquefaction; fluid input/gas output selects vaporization. Configure ports before hammering the structure.

The GUI can switch direction, update ports and reset current progress. Check resources and stored contents before interrupting a running batch.

Recipes define mappings, ratios, duration and energy. Sulfuric acid vapor now liquefies at 1000 mB to 1000 mB, 100 ticks and 40 FE/t. Other mappings require matching data packs; fluids and gases remain separate resources.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.storage.title: Stores and ports
tutorial.alone_mechanical.storage.body:
Place storage before connecting pipes. Vaults hold items; tanks hold fluids or gases. Matching storage stacks vertically only. Each vault adds 27 slots and each tank adds 16000 mB. Keep resource types separate; empty a tank before changing its phase.

Ports are the machine inventory doors. Put them directly above or below a column and use the wrench to cycle Input 1, Input 2, Output 1 and Output 2. One column uses one channel, so Input 1 and Input 2 need separate columns.

Right-click a standalone store for its GUI. In a formed machine, sneak-right-click opens the store view and normal right-click opens the machine. If nothing moves, check the channel, pipe mode and destination space in that order.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.pipes.title: Pipes and faces
tutorial.alone_mechanical.pipes.body:
Remember one sentence: pull from the source, receive at the destination. Item, fluid and gas pipes are separate. Tier 1–5 move 4/16/64/128/256 items per second, or 4000/16000/64000/128000/256000 mB per second for fluids and gases.

A normal connection receives and forwards. To make a pipe draw from storage, sneak-right-click its arm with the wrench and choose Pull. Choose Push when it should actively send to a target. Blue collars pull, orange collars push, and None disconnects that face.

Branches share the trunk budget and mixed tiers run at the slowest segment. Full destinations are skipped. Fluid and gas pipes buffer 1000 mB per segment and resume when the chunk is loaded.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.upgrades.title: Coils and matrices
tutorial.alone_mechanical.upgrades.body:
Machine upgrade parts have no separate count cap; available structure space is the limit. Each energy coil subtracts 20%% of base energy additively, with a minimum 1 FE/t per recipe. Each efficiency coil adds 15%% speed and 10%% energy multiplier.

Each processing matrix adds one parallel slot: 1/2/3 matrices allow 2/3/4 recipes. Each also adds 15%% energy multiplier. All upgrades add to the same base: multiplier = max(0, 1 - 0.20 x energy coils + 0.10 x efficiency coils + 0.15 x processing matrices). Round each recipe up to at least 1 FE/t. Total power scales again with the actual batch. Inputs and output capacity lock the batch at cycle start; late inputs cannot enlarge it.

Energy matrix capacity is unchanged. Base battery: %s FE; machine capacity = base × (1 + energy matrices). Removing cells clamps excess energy.

After upgrades or repairs, hammer-click any block within the old machine to recheck its saved bounds. This resets processing progress while preserving physical resources and energy within capacity. First builds and expansions still use opposite corners; Shift-click to cancel, then select new corners, including inside the old bounds.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.help.title: GUI and troubleshooting
tutorial.alone_mechanical.help.body:
Formation failed: read the chat reason and position first. Then check the closed cuboid, one controller, the core and component touching, and at least one energy matrix.

No transfer: confirm both sides use the same resource type, Pull is set at the source, the target has the correct input channel and both stores have room.

No processing: read the machine GUI status, inputs, outputs and FE. Pylon coverage is checked at the core; changing a recipe or direction resets progress.

Cannot find a recipe: search the output directly in JEI. The guide explains how to operate machines; JEI remains the source for ingredients, amounts and data-pack recipes.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.builds.title: Machine build examples
tutorial.alone_mechanical.builds.body:
All processing and generating multiblocks share one industrial core, anywhere inside the selection or on its surface. Place the listed component directly above it, also inside the selection. Keep a complete shell, one surface controller, an energy matrix and independent storage columns with universal ports directly above/below them.

Administrator examples: /AloneMechanical build +structure
crusher: crushing component, item input/output.
arc_furnace: calcination component, item input/output.
forging_press: forging component, item input/output.
forming_machine: forming component, item input/output.
infuser: infusion component; item + fluid/gas to item.
alloy_smelter: alloy component; main item + auxiliary input to item.
reaction: compound component; Input 1, Input 2, Output 1; storage media select nine profiles.
separator: decomposition component; Input 1, Output 1, Output 2.
converter: conversion component; two tanks, choose direction in the GUI.
boiler: boiler component; water, hot carrier, steam, cooled carrier.
turbine: turbine component; horizontal contiguous rotors and matrix on the same X/Z axis, steam Input 1.
nuclear_reactor: four horizontal fuel rods adjacent to the actual core, no upper component; fuel, coolant, waste, hot medium tanks.
slaughterhouse / breeding_tower / harvest_tower / repeller_tower: corresponding field component, 3x3 footprint and item Output 1; breeding also needs food Input 1.

Hammer opposite corners. Pylons cover the actual industrial core, which also anchors field ranges. Single-block generators, pumps and standalone storage matrices retain their own construction rules.

Tower examples: /AloneMechanical build +distillation_tower, +condensation_tower, +exchange_tower. See Process Towers for construction details.

Air separation tower: industrial core + air separation component, minimum 5x5x7, open top, casing floor/frame, wall controller and energy matrix. Output 1 nitrogen / Output 2 oxygen only, no inputs or tanks. Newly formed towers start switched off; enable in the GUI and supply FE. Each recipe yields 400 mB N2 + 100 mB O2 in 100 ticks at base 20 FE/t per recipe. Volume slider scales batches and actual FE. Either full output pauses the whole batch. Switch and buffers persist. Command: /AloneMechanical build +air_separation_tower.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.separation.bod:
The industrial core + compound component with a decomposition component directly above performs independent one-input, two-output recipes. Use a central industrial core + compound component with a decomposition component directly above, complete casing, one controller and at least one energy matrix. Hammer-right-click opposite corners to form; sneak-right-click cancels.

Exactly three independent storage columns: Input 1, Output 1 and Output 2. Use item vaults or tanks with ports directly above or below. Input 2 must be absent. The GUI shows one input on the left and two protected outputs on the right.

The storage media select eighteen profiles, including sorting, pyrolytic separation, liquid fractionation, degassing, electrolysis and gas fractionation. Different output media may swap channels; matching media follow recipe order. Empty tanks prepare the output phase for a matching recipe.

Water electrolysis: water on Input 1, separate gas stores on Output 1 and Output 2. 1000 mB water → 1000 mB hydrogen + 500 mB oxygen; 200 ticks at 60 FE/t. With universal tanks, insert water first; empty output tanks adopt the gas phase automatically.

A full or incompatible output pauses processing. Both outputs are checked before completion. Coils and batteries are supported; each processing matrix adds one parallel slot and 15%% energy multiplier; input and both output capacities limit the batch. Data packs define additional decomposition recipes independently.

Same-phase decomposition: item → item + item; fluid → fluid + fluid; gas → gas + gas. Each uses independent Input 1, Output 1 and Output 2 columns and recipes, never automatically reversed reaction recipes.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.pumps.title: Electric pump
tutorial.alone_mechanical.pumps.body:
The electric pump is a single-block machine. Place it directly; no casing, core or hammer is required.

Intake: only the block touching its bottom is checked. Each water/lava source supplies 1000 mB per cycle. Ordinary flowing liquid is skipped. Waterlogged blocks use bucket pickup behavior and retain the host block. The pump does not search nearby pools or create liquid.

Power: cover the pump position with a pylon, or supply FE directly on any face. Base battery uses the machine battery config. Base cycle: 20 ticks (1 second), 40 FE/t; internal fluid buffer: 16000 mB.

Upgrades: right-click and place blocks in their matching GUI slots. Up to 64 efficiency coils each add 15%% speed and 10%% energy multiplier. Up to 64 energy coils each subtract 20%% of base cost, minimum 1 FE/t. Up to 64 energy matrices each add one base battery capacity. Changing upgrades resets progress; removing battery matrices clamps energy to the new capacity. Processing matrices are reserved for recipe multiblocks.

Output: connect top/side fluid pipes and set their source face to Pull. Bottom is intake only. The buffer rejects external filling. Full/incompatible fluid buffers or low energy pause work. Hover the tank, battery and upgrade slots for details. Breaking the pump drops its installed upgrade blocks.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.energy_storage:
An independent multiblock battery needs no machine core or controller. Build a complete cuboid boundary from machine casings, reinforced casings or structural glass, with at least one energy matrix. Interior air is allowed. Coils, processing matrices, storage and ports are rejected.

Select opposite corners with the engineering hammer; sneak-click cancels. Each dimension is 3 to %s blocks. Each cell provides %s FE; all members share %s FE/t input and output limits independently. Right-click any member for the same GUI.

Charge only stores the core buffer and cannot discharge. Discharge only rejects charging and supplies demand. Dynamic balance stores current-tick generation surplus and supplies core shortages on demand without idle cycling. Modes also constrain direct FE capabilities.

Cover the geometric center with a pylon linked to a grid core, or use direct FE on any solid member. The GUI shows this matrix, total grid input/output and net flow in FE/t, measured during the previous completed tick. Hover the grid for external generation/demand and all storage transfers.

Damage immediately disables the structure while retaining its single stored battery for repair and re-forming. Removing every energy cell clears it. Unloaded chunks suspend operation. Re-forming or expanding transfers energy once; capacity reduction discards excess.
jei.alone_mechanical.energy_storage: Energy matrices also form standalone multiblock batteries with casings, reinforced casings and structural glass. Use a complete boundary and select opposite corners with the engineering hammer; no core or controller. Its GUI offers charge-only, discharge-only and balance modes, plus grid flow readings. Cover the structure center with a pylon or use direct FE. See the Energy storage tutorial chapter.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.goggles.title: Engineering goggles
tutorial.alone_mechanical.goggles.body:
Equip the engineering goggles in the head slot. Rebind the goggles controls in Options → Controls → Key Binds → Engineering goggles; the following keys are defaults. Y enters overview aligned to the nearest cardinal heading. Left/Right arrows turn the view by 90° per press, without key-repeat turns. Press Y again to restore the original view; player look is unchanged. Game mode and flight permissions remain unchanged.

Tap and release Left Shift to toggle the free camera. WASD pans the camera while the player stays horizontally still. Tap Left Shift again to return to player-centered overview.

Hold Left Shift and press WASD to move the player instead. This exits free camera and follows the player; releasing this chord does not toggle free view again. Ordinary follow view also permits WASD movement. Scroll adjusts height from 8 to 64 blocks. Free panning stays within 48 blocks of the player.

Formed machines display whole-structure bounds and labels: type, size, energy, required FE/t, state, speed and parallel capacity. Labels require worn goggles: look at a machine or hold the hammer in normal view; overview shows nearby loaded machines. Removing goggles hides all labels immediately. Text always faces the camera. Panels are scaled to 80% with a thin teal border. F7 toggles all goggles overlays while camera controls remain active. Storage matrices show capacity and discharge too.

Leaving a world, changing dimension, death or removing the goggles exits overview. Menus pause panning. Craft goggles with leather, copper ingots and glass panes.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.boiler.title: Boiler and Heat Carrier
tutorial.alone_mechanical.boiler.body:
Place a industrial core + boiler component anywhere in the selection, with the component directly above the core. Minimum 3x3x3 cuboid: complete shell, one surface controller and at least one energy matrix. Select opposite corners with the hammer.

Exactly four independent tank columns, with universal ports above or below: water Input 1, superheated carrier Input 2, steam Output 1, cooled carrier Output 2. No item vaults or shared channels. Empty Output 1 tanks prepare for steam automatically.

50 mB water + 1 mB hot carrier -> 50 mB steam + 1 mB cooled carrier in 1 tick (0.05 s). Heat comes from the hot fluid; no FE is needed by default. Cooled carrier cannot supply heat again directly. Cooled fluid is sky-blue/gray; hot fluid is orange/gray. Both use animated water textures. Carrier uses fluid pipes; steam uses gas pipes.

Either blocked output pauses the entire batch without consuming inputs or creating a partial product. Speed coils and processing matrices are supported; quantities scale with the actual batch, with progress and batches saved. Sodium is produced by brine processing and molten salt electrolysis, then heated by reactors. Carrier has no dedicated bucket; use tanks and fluid pipes for storage and transfer.
jei.alone_mechanical.boiler: industrial core + boiler component; minimum 3x3x3 cuboid, complete casing, one controller and an energy matrix. Four top/bottom ports: water Input 1, hot carrier Input 2, steam Output 1, cooled carrier Output 2. 50+1 mB -> 50+1 mB, 1 tick (0.05 s), no FE by default. Either blocked output pauses the entire batch.

Use an industrial core with a reactor fuel rod directly north, south, east and west at the same height. No component above the core. Minimum 3x3x3 cuboid, complete shell, one surface controller and at least one energy matrix. Select opposite corners with the hammer.

Four independent tank columns with ports above/below: Input 1 liquid fuel, Input 2 water or heat carrier, Output 1 liquid nuclear waste, Output 2 steam gas or superheated liquid carrier. Channels cannot share columns. Vertical tanks add capacity; empty Output 2 adopts the recipe phase.

Every 1 tick (0.05 s): 1 mB fuel + 50 mB water -> 1 mB waste + 50 mB steam; or 1 mB fuel + 50 mB carrier -> 1 mB waste + 50 mB superheated carrier. No FE cost or direct FE generation. Send steam to turbines and hot carrier to boilers.

Enriched uranium fuel is green, MOX orange, thorium cyan and waste brown-yellow. All are real fluids using animated water textures. Old fuel rod items are removed; the structural fuel rod blocks are not consumed. Fuel preparation and waste recovery are available; see Nuclear Fuel Preparation and Recovery. Thorium requires heavy water.

Missing inputs, full waste or blocked heated output pauses the whole batch without input loss or partial output. Broken structures stop. Overheating can cause fuel-dependent explosions and radiation; see Sodium Cooling and Reactor Safety. Data packs can adjust all six default processing recipes.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.towers.title: Process Towers
tutorial.alone_mechanical.towers.body:
All three towers require width/depth at least 5 and height at least 7, up to the machine axis limit. Floors and all frame edges must be machine/reinforced casings. Complete side walls may contain glass, controller, energy matrices, coils and universal ports.

Use one industrial core, with a distillation/condensation/exchange component directly above it. They may be off-center, but cannot replace floor, frame or divider casings. One wall controller and an energy matrix are required.

Distillation / condensation: keep the entire top interior open, with a casing rim. Wall Input 1 and Output 1 connect directly to internal buffers; distillation optionally uses Output 2. No storage tanks. Distillation takes liquid and yields recipe-defined fluid/gas products; condensation takes gas and yields liquid.

Exchange: seal the roof and separate two chambers with exactly one complete casing plane. Leave interior space above/below. Lower chamber uses Input 1 / Output 1, upper uses Input 2 / Output 2, with separate buffers for fluids or gases.

Only internal air between floor and roof contributes volume. Each block adds 1000 mB per channel in its chamber. A 5x5x7 open tower has 45 blocks; a central exchange divider leaves 18 per chamber. Right-click and use the 1–100% batch-volume slider. Whole recipes round down; a budget smaller than one recipe waits. FE scales with actual recipe count; coils still apply.

Examples: 1000 mB water -> 950 mB steam + 50 mB enriched water, 100 ticks, 40 FE/t, requiring Output 2; steam 1000 mB -> water 1000 mB, 100 ticks, 20 FE/t. Exchange: 50 mB water + 1 mB hot carrier -> 50 mB steam + 1 mB cooled carrier, 1 tick at 20 FE/t per recipe. Missing inputs, power or any output room pauses the whole batch.

Quick builds: /AloneMechanical build +distillation_tower, +condensation_tower, +exchange_tower. Configure ports, then hammer opposite corners. Pylons default to 15x15 and check the actual industrial core.

Air separation tower: industrial core + air separation component, minimum 5x5x7, open top, casing floor/frame, wall controller and energy matrix. Output 1 nitrogen / Output 2 oxygen only, no inputs or tanks. Newly formed towers start switched off; enable in the GUI and supply FE. Each recipe yields 400 mB N2 + 100 mB O2 in 100 ticks at base 20 FE/t per recipe. Volume slider scales batches and actual FE. Either full output pauses the whole batch. Switch and buffers persist. Command: /AloneMechanical build +air_separation_tower.

Tower operation: intensity scales batch volume and multiplies FE per recipe by 1 + intensity percentage (2x at 100%). Air separation yields 400 mB N2 + 100 mB O2 per 100 ticks at base 20 FE/t; its default batch budget is 100 mB/m3, while storage stays 1000 mB/m3. Every gas output offers Keep / Vent excess / Vent all; Keep pauses when full.

Liquid levels follow actual buffers, visible through the opening/glass, with separate display regions for Input 1/Output 1/Output 2. Distinct feeds select recipes: water -> steam/enriched water; saline raw water -> water/brine; brine -> molten salt/steam. No mode switch. All three require Output 2; either blocked outlet pauses the batch. Add Output 2 and recheck old single-output towers; quick builds include it.

tooltip.alone_mechanical.item.sulfur.inf: React 1 coal or charcoal with 1000 mB water for 1 sulfur. Oxidize with oxygen to SO2, then oxidize, hydrate with steam and liquefy to sulfuric acid.
Five stages: sulfur recovery, oxidation, contact oxidation, steam hydration and liquefaction. All recipes appear in JEI. Reactors use an industrial core with a compound component directly above; storage media select the profile.

1. 1 coal OR charcoal + 1000 mB water -> 1 sulfur. Item Input 1, water Input 2, item Output 1: Crystallization. 200 ticks, 40 FE/t. This first stage is a gameplay abstraction and yields sulfur only.

2. 1 sulfur + 1000 mB oxygen -> 1000 mB sulfur dioxide. Item Input 1, gas Input 2, gas Output 1: Solid Gasification. 100 ticks, 40 FE/t.

3. 1000 mB SO2 + 500 mB oxygen -> 1000 mB SO3. Three separate gas columns: Gas-Phase Synthesis. 160 ticks, 60 FE/t. Ratio follows 2SO2 + O2 -> 2SO3; catalyst beds and temperature control are abstracted into the reactor process. No catalyst consumable.

4. 1000 mB SO3 + 1000 mB steam -> 1000 mB sulfuric acid vapor. Gas-Phase Synthesis, with SO3 on Input 1 and steam on Input 2. 120 ticks, 60 FE/t. Requires steam gas, not liquid water.

5. 1000 mB acid vapor -> 1000 mB liquid acid. Industrial core + gas-liquid conversion component; select Gas to Liquid in the GUI. Gas Input 1 and liquid Output 1. 100 ticks, 40 FE/t.

Supply oxygen from an enabled air separation tower or by water electrolysis in a separator; obtain steam from a water distillation tower or boiler. Attach universal ports directly above/below independent storage columns. Use gas pipes for oxygen, steam and sulfur gases; fluid pipes for water and liquid acid.

Equal-type gas inputs must follow JEI channel order. Blocked output pauses without consuming inputs. Coils and processing matrices apply. Portable tanks and sampling tools transport acid. tutorial.alone_mechanical.heavy_water.bo:
Two routes produce heavy water. Amounts below are per recipe; 20 ticks = 1 second. Listed FE is before coils, parallel batches and tower intensity.

Route 1: water -> enriched water -> heavy water.
1. Distillation tower: Input 1 takes 1000 mB water; Output 1 gives 950 mB steam and Output 2 gives 50 mB enriched water. 100 ticks, 40 FE/t. Water has one co-production recipe and requires the wall Output 2 port. Port count no longer selects a different recipe.
2. Twenty batches accumulate 1000 mB enriched water. Build a separator with an industrial core and decomposition component directly above it, plus three separate liquid storage columns. Input 1: 1000 mB enriched water -> Output 1: 900 mB water + Output 2: 100 mB heavy water. 200 ticks, 60 FE/t.
3. Recycle separated water. Steam can fuel a turbine or condense in 1000 mB batches to recover 1000 mB water (100 ticks, 20 FE/t). Unwanted steam may use Vent excess or Vent all on distillation Output 1 to prevent it blocking enrichment.

Route 2: hydrogen -> deuterium -> heavy water steam -> heavy water.
1. Use a decomposition-component separator with three independent gas columns. Input 1: 1000 mB hydrogen -> Output 1: 990 mB hydrogen + Output 2: 10 mB deuterium. 200 ticks, 120 FE/t. Recycle hydrogen with fresh makeup. Vent all discards recoverable hydrogen.
2. Use a compound-component reactor with three gas columns. Input 1: 1000 mB deuterium + Input 2: 500 mB oxygen -> Output 1: 1000 mB heavy water steam. 100 ticks, 80 FE/t. Follow channel order; accumulate 1000 mB deuterium first.
3. Condensation tower: Input 1 takes 1000 mB heavy water steam -> Output 1 gives 1000 mB heavy water. 100 ticks, 40 FE/t. Air separation supplies oxygen; water electrolysis supplies hydrogen.

Construction and transport: distillation/condensation require a 5x5x7 minimum open-top tower, casing floor/frame and direct wall ports without attached tanks. Separator/reactor channels need independent storage columns with ports directly above/below. Fluid pipes carry water, enriched water and heavy water. Gas pipes carry hydrogen, oxygen, deuterium and both steam types. Empty universal tanks select phase from incoming media; one column cannot mix phases.

Operation: Keep internally is default; a blocked required output pauses the whole batch. Each gas output offers Keep / Vent excess / Vent all; liquid outputs still need room. Higher tower intensity increases batches and multiplies FE per recipe by 1 + intensity percentage (2x at 100%), before machine upgrades. The GUI shows actual FE/t. Ratios are gameplay parameters.

Iron, copper and gold yields are ingots per raw ore. Intermediate and advanced routes share clump crushing. Dust always smelts 1:1.

Basic 2x: 1 raw ore -> crusher -> 2 dust -> smelt -> 2 ingots. 100 ticks, 20 FE/t.

Intermediate 3x: 1 raw ore + 200 mB oxygen -> infuser purification -> 3 clumps (160 ticks, 40 FE/t). Crush each into 1 dust (60 ticks, 20 FE/t), then smelt. Total: 200 mB oxygen and 10000 FE per raw ore before smelting. Item Input 1, oxygen gas Input 2, clump Output 1.

Advanced 5x: 1 raw ore + 1000 mB liquid acid -> Dissolution -> 1000 mB crude slurry (200 ticks, 80 FE/t). Add 1000 mB water in Liquid-Phase Synthesis -> 2000 mB washed slurry (160 ticks, 60 FE/t). Slurry Separation -> 5 crystals + 1000 mB mother liquor (240 ticks, 100 FE/t). Each crystal + 200 mB hydrogen -> Gas-Solid Refining -> 1 clump (100 ticks, 80 FE/t). Crush the five clumps through the same 1:1 tail and smelt for 5 ingots.

Recovery: fractionate 1000 mB mother liquor into 500 mB acid + 500 mB water (160 ticks, 80 FE/t). Startup needs 1000 mB acid and water; net advanced use is 500 mB acid, 500 mB water and 1000 mB hydrogen per raw ore. Total 108400 FE before smelting and upstream production. Useful mother liquor is retained; no extra waste fluid.

Clumps are compact mineral aggregates, crystals single faceted prisms: silver-gray iron, orange copper, yellow gold. Existing concentrates and crystals adopt the new names, art and uses.

Use existing industrial cores and crushing, infusion, compound and decomposition components. Reactors have two inputs/one output; separators one input/two outputs. Keep storage columns independent. Purification infusers need a gas tank; shard washing needs a liquid tank. Missing resources or blocked outputs pause safely. Coils, parallel matrices and saved progress apply.

Clumps, crystals, dust and ingots cannot restart multiplication. Intermediates cannot smelt directly. Only advanced slurry produces mother liquor. Shared crushing is 1:1, never another multiplier. JEI labels shared steps separately.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.nuclear_fuel.b:
Uranium ore generates in Overworld biomes at Y=-64 to 64, with 8 vein attempts per chunk and vein size 8. Triangular height distribution peaks near Y=0. It is intended to be rarer than iron and more common than gold in ordinary biomes; vanilla Badlands gold bonuses remain. Stone and deepslate generate their matching uranium ore variants. Existing saves need newly generated chunks; old chunks are not retroactively populated. Use an iron-or-better pickaxe for raw uranium; Silk Touch preserves ore and Fortune applies.

Enriched uranium: crush 1 raw uranium into 2 dust. Dissolve 4 uranium dust with 1000 mB liquid sulfuric acid into 1000 mB uranium slurry (200 ticks, 80 FE/t). Liquid Precipitation separates 1000 mB slurry into Output 1: 1 enriched uranium compound and Output 2: 3 depleted uranium dust (240 ticks, 100 FE/t). Dissolve 1 enriched compound with 1000 mB water into 1000 mB enriched uranium fuel (120 ticks, 80 FE/t).

Recovery: accumulate 1000 mB reactor waste and use Liquid Precipitation for Output 1: 1 recovered fuel pellet and Output 2: 9 sealed nuclear waste (300 ticks, 120 FE/t). Solid-Phase Synthesis combines 1 recovered pellet with 3 depleted dust into 1 mixed fuel compound (160 ticks, 80 FE/t). Dissolve it with 1000 mB water for 1000 mB MOX fuel (120 ticks, 80 FE/t). New depleted uranium is still required; sealed waste has no fuel recycling recipe.

Thorium and heavy water: Crystallization converts 4 depleted uranium dust + 100 mB heavy water into 4 thorium dust (200 ticks, 60 FE/t). Heavy water is consumed. Dissolve 4 thorium dust with 1000 mB water for 1000 mB thorium fuel (120 ticks, 60 FE/t). Use either existing heavy-water route. Ordinary or enriched water cannot replace heavy water in conversion. This is a gameplay conversion and needs no new ore.

Reactors use an industrial core with a compound component above; separators use a decomposition component. Separate physical storage columns select the profile. Separator Output 1/2 require independent item vaults; either blocked output pauses the entire batch. Finished liquid fuels use reactor Input 1; Input 2 remains water or heat carrier. All recipes appear in JEI. Raw uranium and uranium dust can also smelt or blast into uranium ingots.

Ingot entry: crusher, 1 uranium ingot -> 1 dust, 100 ticks, 20 FE/t; or Dissolution, 4 ingots + 1000 mB sulfuric acid -> 1000 mB uranium slurry, 240 ticks, 100 FE/t. Both feed uranium enrichment, depleted-uranium thorium conversion and MOX waste recovery. Ingot grinding is 1:1.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.reactor_safety:
Sodium cooling is inspired by real sodium-cooled fast reactors. Volumes, yields and temperatures are gameplay parameters. Legacy carrier registry IDs remain compatible.

Dissolution: gravel 1 + water 1000 mB -> saline raw water 1000 mB, 100 ticks, 40 FE/t. Distillation: saline raw water 1000 mB -> water 900 mB + brine 100 mB, 200 ticks, 60 FE/t. Gravel leaching is a gameplay abstraction; recycle water into the leaching reactor.
Distillation: brine 1000 mB -> molten sodium chloride 200 mB (Output 1) + steam 800 mB (Output 2), 200 ticks, 120 FE/t.
Degassing Separation: molten salt 1000 mB -> sodium 500 mB (Output 1) + chlorine 500 mB (Output 2), 200 ticks, 160 FE/t. Store chlorine or vent it using gas output settings.

Reactors heat sodium; boilers/exchange towers transfer heat to water, returning cold sodium. Water and sodium remain separate. Sodium-water chemical accidents are not simulated. Water cooling remains available.

GUI shows temperature, decay activity and SCRAM. Defaults: automatic SCRAM at 600 C; 1200 C or high loop pressure starts a 5 second countdown, and cooling can still prevent the accident. Shutdown or missing fuel does not remove decay heat. Keep coolant Input 2 and hot Output 2 available. Residual cooling converts 10 mB coolant/tick without waste. Blocked waste stops burning; blocked hot output also stops residual cooling.

Base blast powers: thorium 6, uranium 8, MOX 12. Changing fuel cannot lower the retained grade before cooling completes. Reinforced casing reduces blasts but the core is still destroyed. Contamination fades over 30 minutes. Breaking a hot controller releases radiation; saves and rebuilding preserve heat.

Hot reactors emit weak radiation; 8 reinforced casings suppress normal leakage. Overheating/damage still leaks. Accumulated dose causes weakness, poison, then wither. Dose recovers 2/sec outside fields; action bar reports exposure. Creative/spectator players are immune. Fields/doses persist without chunk forcing. Server config controls hazards, temperatures, powers and lifetime.

Stage 1: craft basic circuits, industrial cores, controllers, matrices, casings, storage and universal ports from iron, copper and redstone. Batteries remain disposable generator fuel: continuous power while burning, then consumed. They are not rechargeable energy containers.

Electrolytes: dissolve 2 sulfur with 1000 mB water into 1000 mB basic electrolyte. Liquid Synthesis combines 1000 basic electrolyte and 1000 sulfuric acid into 2000 intermediate electrolyte. Liquid Absorption combines 1000 intermediate electrolyte and 1000 ammonia gas into 2000 advanced electrolyte. Use independent input columns matching each phase.

Infuser: industrial core with infusion component above; Input 1 item vault, Input 2 liquid tank, Output 1 item vault. Attach top/bottom ports and set channels. One basic casing + 250 basic electrolyte makes one basic battery; one intermediate casing + 500 intermediate electrolyte makes one intermediate battery; one advanced casing + 1000 advanced electrolyte makes one advanced battery. Wrong tiers, shortages and blocked outputs consume nothing.

Advanced reprocessing: dissolve 4 redstone with 1000 advanced electrolyte into 1000 high-power conditioning fluid; dissolve 4 quartz sand with 1000 advanced electrolyte into 1000 long-life stabilizing fluid. Infuse one finished advanced battery with 250 conditioning fluid into a high-power battery, or with 250 stabilizing fluid into a long-life battery. Both consume a finished advanced battery; empty casings cannot directly produce variants. High-power: 1.5x power, 0.7x duration of advanced. Long-life: 1x power, 1.5x duration.

Basic/intermediate/advanced power and duration scale by 1/2/4. Emergency batteries have a separate handmade potato, copper and redstone recipe.

tutorial.alone_mechanical.pipe_tools.bod: The pipe filter chip creates an item whitelist: put the sample item in the offhand and right-click an item pipe; sneak-right-click clears it. The server checks and saves the filter before transfer. A priority chip raises priority with a normal right-click and lowers it while sneaking, from -8 to +8; higher-priority branches receive material first, while equal branches remain round-robin. Use a maintenance battery pack with a damaged damageable item in the other hand to repair 64 durability per pack.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.grid_tools.bod:
Signal poles are 9 blocks tall and power pylons are 7 blocks tall; wire anchors sit at their tops. The zipline hook works only between two loaded signal poles with a direct PowerGridData edge: right-click the first, then the second. The server controls travel; sneaking, disconnection, unloaded chunks, death or dimension changes detach safely. The hook has durability and pylons are not ride anchors.

Right-click a node with the grid analyzer to show node type, link count, core position, cached FE and supply state.
tutorial.alone_mechanical.synthesis.body:
Place the synthesis component directly above an industrial core to form a directed synthesizer. It uses two independent item columns: Item Input 1 for the ingredients of a crafting recipe and Item Output 1 for the result. Shell, ports, energy matrices and power coverage follow the other industrial machines.

The synthesizer reads the server's current RecipeManager crafting list. The left and right GUI buttons select only a server-authorized target; the target id is saved on the block entity. After a datapack reload, an invalid target is discarded and the list is refreshed. Missing inputs, a blocked output or insufficient energy pause safely without consuming materials.

The basic machine route starts with machine casing. Structural glass is a further casing recipe using glass and iron nuggets. JEI shows the machine family, technology stage and required top component; use R/U to follow inputs and downstream uses.
